reagents.name: LiAlH4 (Lithium Aluminium Hydride)
reagents.function: Powerful reducing agent; reduces aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acids, and amides to alcohols/amines.

reagents.name: PCC (Pyridinium Chlorochromate)
reagents.function: Mild oxidising agent in anhydrous CH2Cl2; selectively oxidises 1° alcohols to aldehydes (avoids over-oxidation to carboxylic acids) and 2° alcohols to ketones.

reagents.name: O3 followed by Zn/H2O (Reductive Ozonolysis)
reagents.function: Cleaves carbon-carbon double bonds oxidatively to form aldehydes and ketones without over-oxidising to carboxylic acids.

reagents.name: mCPBA (meta-Chloroperoxybenzoic Acid)
reagents.function: Epoxidation of alkenes via syn-addition; also used in Baeyer-Villiger oxidation of ketones to esters.

named_reactions.name: Aldol Condensation
named_reactions.reactants: Aldehydes or ketones containing α-hydrogens in the presence of dilute base (NaOH) or acid with heat.
named_reactions.products: α,β-Unsaturated aldehyde or ketone via dehydration of β-hydroxy intermediate (e.g., 2 CH3CHO -> But-2-enal + H2O).

named_reactions.name: Cannizzaro Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Non-enolisable aldehydes (no α-hydrogens, e.g., Formaldehyde, Benzaldehyde) treated with concentrated alkali (50% KOH).
named_reactions.products: Equimolar redox disproportionation mixture of a 1° alcohol and a carboxylic acid salt (e.g., 2 PhCHO -> PhCH2OH + PhCOOK).

named_reactions.name: Friedel-Crafts Alkylation / Acylation
named_reactions.reactants: Benzene or activated aromatic ring + Alkyl/Acyl halide in the presence of anhydrous Lewis acid (AlCl3, FeBr3).
named_reactions.products: Alkylbenzene or aryl ketone + HX (e.g., Benzene + CH3COCl / AlCl3 -> Acetophenone + HCl).

named_reactions.name: Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
named_reactions.reactants: Primary aliphatic or aromatic amide + Br2 in aqueous or ethanolic NaOH / KOH.
named_reactions.products: Primary amine with one fewer carbon atom + Na2CO3 + 2 NaBr + 2 H2O (e.g., CH3CONH2 + Br2/KOH -> CH3NH2).

basic_rules.definition: In β-elimination (E1/E2) reactions of alkyl halides or alcohols, the predominant alkene product is the most substituted, thermodynamically stable alkene (having the greatest number of alkyl substituents attached to the sp2 carbons).

In electrophilic addition of an unsymmetrical reagent (HX) to an unsymmetrical alkene, the acidic proton adds to the double-bonded carbon bearing more hydrogen atoms, yielding the more stable carbocation intermediate.

A planar, monocyclic, fully conjugated ring system is aromatic if it possesses (4n + 2) π-electrons (where n is a non-negative integer: 0, 1, 2, 3...). Rings with 4n π-electrons are anti-aromatic and especially unstable.

Substituents on chiral carbons or geometric double bonds are ranked by atomic number of directly attached atoms. Higher atomic number gets higher priority. Used to determine absolute R/S configurations and E/Z isomerism.

core_concepts.core_rule: SN2 is a concerted, bimolecular mechanism favoured by strong nucleophiles, primary substrates, and polar aprotic solvents (Walden inversion). SN1 is a two-step, unimolecular mechanism via carbocation favoured by tertiary substrates, polar protic solvents, and weak nucleophiles (racemisation).
core_concepts.exception: Neopentyl halides are primary but cannot undergo SN2 due to severe steric congestion from the β-quaternary carbon. Allylic and benzylic substrates readily undergo both SN1 and SN2.
core_concepts.keywords: Walden inversion · carbocation · steric hindrance · polar aprotic · polar protic · transition state

core_concepts.core_rule: Electron-donating groups (EDGs: -OH, -NH2, -OCH3, -CH3) activate the benzene ring by increasing electron density (resonance/hyperconjugation) and direct incoming electrophiles to ortho and para positions. Electron-withdrawing groups (EWGs: -NO2, -CN, -COOH) deactivate and direct meta.
core_concepts.exception: Halogens (-F, -Cl, -Br, -I) deactivate the ring through strong inductive electron withdrawal (-I) yet direct ortho/para due to weak resonance donation (+M) of lone pairs.
core_concepts.keywords: sigma complex · arenium ion · ortho/para director · meta director · activating · deactivating · halogen anomaly

core_concepts.core_rule: Carbocation intermediates spontaneously rearrange via 1,2-hydride or 1,2-alkyl (methyl/phenyl) shifts whenever the shift transforms a less stable carbocation (1° or 2°) into a more stable one (3° or resonance-stabilised allylic/benzylic).
core_concepts.exception: Ring expansion (e.g., cyclobutylcarbinyl to cyclopentyl carbocation) provides additional thermodynamic driving force by relieving severe ring strain in 4-membered rings.
core_concepts.keywords: 1,2-hydride shift · 1,2-methyl shift · Wagner-Meerwein · ring expansion · thermodynamic stability
